sweep_summary: The sweep for Galela (gale1259) turned up only two title hits, and they are one work: Shelden's 'Galela phonemes and stress' (WILC 7, 1989, pp. 77-88; Glottolog 111944) and the CLDF/StressTyp2-derived duplicate record 686214 that mis-dates it as '1990, vol. 8' (the held WILC vol. 8 contains no Galela paper). This is already the catalog's deciding source and was already held on file as an image-only PDF plus scanned; I re-rendered and read the page images for p. 78 and p. 85 and read the scanned of sec. 4.1-4.3: stress is on the penultimate syllable of the stem, monomorphemic words are penult, loan antepenults are analysed as underlying penult plus vowel paragogue, and 'Stress placement is not affected by affixation' (/no-tagi-kasi/, ['?umokasi]). Both items confirm the catalog's 'morphological' (stem-penult) coding; nothing new to acquire from the title sweep. The held PDF and scanned were copied into with and a note. Outside the sweep's item list, the only unheld corroborating sources remain van Baarda 1908 (HathiTrust full view hvd.hx4vpm, but babel.hathitrust.org still returns 403 from our machine) and the 1989 Galela conversations book (HathiTrust search-only); both are low priority and would at most corroborate Shelden.

new_statements.quote: Stress is predictable on the penultimate syllable of stems and will not be marked on words written phonemically. [p. 78] ... 4.3. Stress and affixation. Stress placement is not affected by affixation. In this respect it differs from neighboring Loloda and Tobelo (van Baarda 1904:356-9) and Tobaru (Fortgens 1928:392ff). In the following examples, the penultimate syllable of tagi is always stressed, regardless of affixes. /wo-tagi/ 'he's walking' (he-walk) /wo-tagi-li/ 'he's walking again' (he-walk-REPET) /no-tagi-kasi/ 'you walk!' (you-walk-IMPERATIVE) /wi-si-tagi-ko/ 'he's forced seawards' (him-CAUS-walk-DIR:sea) [p. 85]

new_statements.locator: p. 78 sec. 1 (PDF p. 87) and p. 85 sec. 4.3 'Stress and affixation' (PDF p. 94); both page images rendered and read
new_statements.reading: Word stress is fixed on the penultimate syllable of the stem (with only apparent antepenult exceptions created by vowel paragogue on loans, which Shelden analyses as underlyingly penult); prefixes and suffixes, including the bound unstressed directional/aspectual suffixes, never attract or shift stress, e.g. ['?umokasi] for /umo-kasi/. This is a stem-domain penult system, i.e. morphologically conditioned rather than word-edge penult, which is exactly the catalog's 'morphological' coding.

audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: every segment of the deciding quotation is present verbatim in the held Shelden 1989 scanned at the stated pages, and the p.78 stem-penult statement plus ['?umokasi] was re-verified on the rendered page image (PDF p.87). (2) The deciding source is a dedicated phonology/stress article by the principal modern fieldworker on Galela, with an explicit stress-and-affixation section; Glottolog lists no later grammar or phonology, and no instrumental/dissertation/JIPA work surfaced. The MORPHOLOGICAL verdict follows directly from Shelden's 'penultimate syllable of stems' + 'Stress placement is not affected by affixation' with /no-tagi-kasi/, /umo-kasi/ ['?umokasi], consistent with catalog precedent for stem-domain penult; the StressTyp2 'P;A' partial mismatch and its wrong 'WILC 8, 1990' citation are already documented in the record. (3) Only low-priority corroborating items remain

sources.note: Stress is on the penultimate syllable of the STEM; monomorphemic words have penult stress; loans with vowel paragogue show surface antepenult stress but are underlyingly penult (Penultimate Stress Rule ordered before the two paragogue rules, sec. 4.1-4.2); affixation (prefixes and suffixes, including directional and aspectual suffixes, note 9: 'phonologically bound, unstressed, and inseparable') does not move stress, so stress is stem-penult, not word-penult. This is the catalog's deciding source and the passages the catalog quotes are present verbatim on the page images.

The held scanned of WILC vol. 8 mentions Galela only once, in a reference list ('Shelden, Howard; Galela Phonology; unpublished'), and carries no Galela article; the paper is in WILC vol. 7 (1989), pp. 77-88. Content and bearing on the catalog identical to item 1.
